statusNote: Nonprofit (Southern Baptist-affiliated) through 2004; sold to investor group and converted to for-profit (Grand Canyon Education, Inc., publicly traded) in 2004; converted back to nonprofit status in 2018, formally recognized by the U.S. Department of Education in December 2025. Brian Mueller has been CEO of the for-profit services company Grand Canyon Education throughout, and separately holds the title President of the (nonprofit) University.

"National & Global" is IWU's adult/online division reporting under the same single president as the main Marion, IN campus (there is no separate president for this division); leadership history below is for Indiana Wesleyan University as a whole.

This IPEDS entity is the flagship/headquarters campus of Keiser University, a private nonprofit university system with numerous branch campuses across Florida and abroad. The institution has been led continuously since its 1977 founding (as The Keiser School, becoming Keiser University in 2006) by co-founder Dr. Arthur Keiser, whose title shifted from President to Chancellor & CEO by 2016. Below Keiser, a separate 'President' role was created circa 2016 to run day-to-day operations of the flagship campus (first Gary Vonk, later others including Ryan Sagers as President of the Fort Lauderdale and Graduate School campuses); those campus-level presidents turn over more frequently and are not well documented for succession purposes, so they are omitted here in favor of the system's top (Chancellor) leader, which is the more relevant role for search-firm tracking. Legal nonprofit parent is Everglades College, Inc. (no formal university 'system' name).
Lamar University became part of the Texas State University System on September 1, 1995 after the Lamar University System (its own separate system) was dissolved by state legislation.

Standalone public university governed by its own Board of Governors (not part of the University of Missouri System). Renamed from Southwest Missouri State University to Missouri State University in 2005; same continuous institution/leadership line.

Founded 1941 as National School of Business; acquired by Harold D. Buckingham in 1962 and renamed National American University in 1997. The physical Rapid City campus closed in 2019 as NAU consolidated to a mostly online delivery model (it retained small on-base sites at Ellsworth AFB, SD and Kings Bay, GA). As of the 2024-2025 catalog the institution is still operating online under Higher Learning Commission accreditation, though enrollment has fallen sharply (~1,600 students) and NAU Holdings (OTC: NAUH) has faced financial distress and Heightened Cash Monitoring status from the Dept. of Education. Named president/CEO succession for 1996-2009 could not be reliably documented; founder-owner Harold D. Buckingham led the institution from 1962 until his death in 1995, and the Buckingham family has remained involved as chairman/board members since.

Also operates a campus in Tampa, FL, and acquired Kendall College (Chicago) in 2018. Complete presidential records between Orley Herron's departure (~1998-1999) and Nivine Megahed's 2010 arrival could not be reliably confirmed via public sources; NLU counts Megahed as its 11th president, implying at least one additional president/leader served in that gap whose name and dates were not identifiable in this research pass.

Founded in 1996 in Prescott Valley, AZ as a for-profit online graduate university. Acquired by the nonprofit National University System (headquartered in La Jolla, CA) in 2019, converting it to nonprofit status, and formally merged into National University in fall 2022 -- Northcentral no longer operates as a separately accredited institution; its academic programs continue under the National University banner. Leadership between founder Donald Hecht's tenure and George Burnett's ~2011 appointment is not fully documented in public sources and may include an unidentified interim leader or gap.

In May 2026 Oakland City University announced it is suspending undergraduate classes for the 2026-2027 academic year amid severe financial distress (missed payroll, all ~167 employees slated for layoff June 1, 2026), while continuing online graduate programs. The university says it hopes to reopen undergraduate programs in Fall 2027, contingent on monetizing a carbon-capture technology patent it holds. Ron Dempsey remained president as of the announcement.

statusNote: Ponce is the main/headquarters campus of the Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Puerto Rico (PUCPR, founded 1948). Unlike the Arecibo and Mayaguez branch campuses, Ponce has no separate campus Rector; it is led directly by the university-wide President, whose succession is recorded here. PUCPR also has a ceremonial 'Grand Chancellor' role held by a Puerto Rico bishop (currently the Bishop of Arecibo); this is a Church-oversight title, not the operating head, so it is not included in the leaders list. Two multi-year gaps in the presidential timeline (circa 1996-1998 and 2002-2006) could not be resolved to a named leader from available public sources.

Purdue Global was created in 2018 when Purdue University acquired the for-profit Kaplan University and converted it into a public, primarily online institution within the Purdue system; leadership history therefore begins in 2018, not 1996.

Regent historically split top leadership between a 'President' (day-to-day CEO) and founder Pat Robertson's 'Chancellor' title (held continuously 1980-2023). Since Carlos Campo's 2013 resignation, the university has not named a separate President; the Chancellor (Pat Robertson, then Gordon Robertson) has functioned as chief executive, with a Provost handling academics. Timeline below reflects the effective top-executive chain, noting each person's actual title.

Formerly part of 'The Sage Colleges' system alongside Sage College of Albany and Sage Graduate School. Effective July 1, 2020, a charter change united Russell Sage College, Sage College of Albany, and Sage Graduate Schools into a single institution under the name Russell Sage College, operating as one college with two co-educational campuses (Troy and Albany, NY). In April 2025 a further merger with Albany College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences was announced, targeted for completion by Fall 2027.

Known as Simmons College until it adopted the Simmons University name in 2018; leadership record below uses one continuous institutional identity.

Knoxville is the flagship campus of a multi-campus institution (additional locations include Asheville, Indianapolis, Dallas, and others), each led locally by a 'campus president' who reports up to the Knoxville-based Chancellor. No institution-wide leadership change has occurred since Stephen A. South's 1989 acquisition; no other names for the top (Chancellor/President) post from 1996-present were found in public sources.

The name of Southeastern's president for the 1996-1998 stretch (immediately before Mark Rutland's January 1999 appointment) could not be reliably identified from accessible sources in this research pass and is omitted rather than guessed; recommend revisiting in a later backfill pass with access to SEU's own institutional archives.

SIUE is one of two campuses (with SIU Carbondale) of the Southern Illinois University System, overseen by a separate SIU System President (currently Daniel F. Mahony, since March 2020); the local campus head, listed below, holds the title Chancellor.
Renamed from St. John Fisher College to St. John Fisher University in 2022; same continuously-led institution throughout.
Private Catholic university sponsored by the Archdiocese of Miami since 1988; standalone institution, not part of a multi-campus system.
Standalone New Jersey state public university (not part of a governing university system); known as Richard Stockton College of New Jersey until 2015.

Small private for-profit online distance-education system (Lakewood, CO/Santa Ana, CA) comprising William Howard Taft University and the separately-run Taft Law School (an unaccredited-by-ABA correspondence law school, split off in 2008 but under common ownership); accredited only by the Distance Education Accrediting Commission, not a traditional research institution. Public leadership records are very sparse online -- only the current and immediate-prior president could be reliably identified; earlier history (this is billed as only the '3rd President' of WHTU) could not be confirmed from public sources despite extensive searching.
In November 2024 the Texas A&M System Board of Regents renamed the institution East Texas A&M University (ETAMU); it remains the same legally and academically continuous institution under a new name.

TWU is a standalone public university (not part of a larger system). Its top leader has held the combined title 'Chancellor and President' since 1999; before that the top title was simply 'President'.
Catholic (Benedictine) college affiliated with the Sisters of St. Scholastica Monastery; standalone institution, not part of a system.

Since 2019 the institution has run a two-tier top-leadership structure: John MacArthur held the newly created title of Chancellor (2019-2025, until his death) as senior spiritual/institutional authority, while a separate President served as chief executive. 'President' is used here as the operating top-leader title; MacArthur's Chancellor role is captured as a note on his entry.

This is Touro's flagship New York institution, founded as Touro College in 1970-71 and renamed Touro University in 2022. It also serves as the headquarters campus for the broader multi-school 'Touro University' system (formerly 'Touro College and University System'), which is distinct from the separately accredited Touro University California and Touro University Nevada. Only two people have led it as president since founding.
Standalone institution affiliated with the Church of the Nazarene denomination (not a multi-campus system).

Owned/operated by the Evangelical Free Church of America (EFCA); the Deerfield, Illinois campus is the main/flagship campus of Trinity International University (which also includes Trinity Law School and other sites), not a branch of a separate outside system.
Standalone Baptist-heritage institution (not part of a formal multi-campus system).

system: Ana G. Méndez University System (formerly Sistema Universitario Ana G. Méndez / SUAGM)
statusNote: This is a campus (Recinto) within the multi-campus Ana G. Méndez University System, alongside the Cupey/Metropolitan and Carolina/Este campuses. It was known as Universidad del Turabo until a systemwide rebrand (~2021-2022) renamed all three campuses under the Ana G. Méndez University banner. Each campus has its own on-site rector (equivalent to a campus president/chancellor) but sits under unified system governance led by a central SUAGM/AGMU system president. IPEDS tracks it as a distinct degree-granting unit, so it is included here, but leadership authority is shared with the parent system.

Complex lineage: this entity descends from Mount St. Clare College (Catholic, Clinton IA) -> The Franciscan University of the Prairies (2003) -> sold to Bridgepoint Education and renamed Ashford University (2005, for-profit, went fully online, Iowa campus closed 2016) -> acquired by the University of Arizona and reconstituted as the nonprofit University of Arizona Global Campus / UAGC (transaction completed Dec 1, 2020). In July 2023 the University of Arizona directly absorbed UAGC (ending its separate nonprofit board/CEO structure), and UAGC is being fully integrated into Arizona Online with a target completion around 2026. Since the 2023 absorption there has been no distinct "UAGC president"; day-to-day leadership has passed through interim SVP and special-advisor roles reporting into University of Arizona central administration (currently President Suresh Garimella, named UA's 23rd president, Oct 2024). Leaders below through 2005 governed the institution under its Mount St. Clare/Franciscan name; from 2005-2020 as Ashford University; from Dec 2020 as UAGC.
Since January 2021, University of Bridgeport has operated as a subsidiary of Goodwin University following Goodwin's acquisition, though UB retains its own name, brand, and board of trustees.
Standalone public university, not part of the University of Arkansas System.
Standalone private university; no parent system.
Formed in 1990 by the merger of University of Detroit and Mercy College of Detroit; sponsored jointly by the Jesuits and Sisters of Mercy. Standalone institution, no parent system.
Standalone private institution, no parent system.
Campus of the University of Hawaii System; led by a chancellor (not president), reporting to the UH System president.
Component institution of the University of Houston System.
Known as Lynchburg College until it was renamed University of Lynchburg in 2018.

Small private, for-profit, online-focused institution (also referred to by its Rosslyn, VA address). Founding president has led the institution continuously since inception; no other presidents on record.
Independent Catholic (Benedictine) university affiliated with the Diocese of Bismarck; not part of a multi-campus system.
Independent Baptist-affiliated university (historically tied to the Baptist General Convention of Texas); not part of a formal multi-campus governing system.

Not a separately-led degree-granting institution for most of the 1996+ window: from 1958 through the mid-2000s this was a division of Chapman University (Division of Residence Education Centers, then the College of Lifelong Learning, renamed Chapman University College in 2001), overseen by a Dean (e.g., Dr. Karen Graham) rather than its own chief executive, and reported to Chapman University's own president. It became a separately accredited institution led by its own chancellor around 2008-2009 when it was renamed Brandman University (funded by a gift from the Joyce and Saul Brandman Foundation). In September 2021 the University of Massachusetts and Chapman University transferred control of Brandman University to UMass, and it was rebranded University of Massachusetts Global -- a nonprofit affiliate of the UMass system rather than one of its traditional public campuses. Leaders below are listed from the point (2007-2009) it gained its own chancellor.
One of three coordinate campuses of the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor, Dearborn, Flint), governed by the same Board of Regents; the campus head carries the title Chancellor, not President.
Standalone public university governed by its own Board of Trustees; not part of the University of Colorado or Colorado State University systems.

IPEDS lists many state-level 'University of Phoenix-XX' location records; this entry (Arizona) is the main/headquarters campus in Phoenix, AZ and its president leads the single accredited University of Phoenix institution as a whole. University of Phoenix was owned by publicly traded Apollo Group / Apollo Education Group through 2017, then acquired by a private-equity consortium (Apollo Global Management, Vistria Group, Najafi Companies) -- this is a corporate ownership structure, not a higher-ed 'system,' so system is left blank. No reliable named source was found for who held the presidency from 1996 to Feb 1998, the gap immediately preceding Jorge Klor de Alva's term; Apollo Group SEC filings from that era are not full-text searchable and no news coverage of that period was located.

Private, historically Presbyterian-affiliated institution; renamed from Pikeville College to University of Pikeville effective July 1, 2011. Standalone, not part of any system. A separate 'Chancellor' title (currently held by Paul E. Patton) exists alongside the presidency, largely an advancement/emeritus-statesman role rather than the chief executive post.
Main campus in St. Paul with a significant Minneapolis downtown campus (including its law school); it is one standalone university, not part of a system.

Small independent health-sciences/chiropractic university (formerly Western States Chiropractic College, renamed 2010). In April 2023 it became an affiliate of The Community Solution (TCS) Education System, a multi-institution nonprofit system, but it retains its own name, brand, campus, and president rather than being absorbed into that system's governance.

Merged into Saint Joseph's University (Philadelphia) effective June 1, 2022, after facing declining enrollment and financial difficulty; ceased to exist as an independently degree-granting institution thereafter. Formerly Philadelphia College of Pharmacy and Science.

For-profit online/distance university, not a traditionally self-governed nonprofit. Majority ownership passed from founders Bernie and Rita Turner to venture capitalist Don Ackerman (1991), to Sylvan Learning Systems/Laureate Education (2001-2021), to current owner Adtalem Global Education (2021-present). The top role has alternated between 'President' and a combined 'CEO' title as corporate structure evolved; entries below reflect whoever held the President title.
Catholic liberal-arts university sponsored by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Youngstown; standalone, no parent system.
